| Melee | 165% (the Defender lower) | `output.factors.melee`: every melee blow a character strikes | none | **×1.35** |
| Sigil, a full Line | 150 to 200% over its turns | `sigils.json grammar.line_mult` | ×1.7 / 1.75 / 1.8 | **×1.87 / 1.93 / 1.98** |
| Outburst, steady / the biggest Release | 135% / 165% | `soul_modules.json damage.base` | 40 | **31** |
| Faith, a Whisper turn / a Hymn turn | 80% / 150% | the prayers' values; `output.profiles.blessing.k` | 1 + 0.1 × Faith | 0.956 × (1 + 0.06 (Virtue − 1) + 0.06 Faith) |
| A healer's turn | 1.25 Soldier-turns | `output.profiles.healing.k` (and `mend`) | 1 + 0.1 (Insight − 1) + 0.1 Empathy | 0.87 × (1 + 0.06 (Insight − 1) + 0.06 Empathy) | *(Superseded by rules 1.27: 2.0 Soldier-turns all in; Healing given 1.392 × (…))*
| Grenades and charges a character throws or sets | the budget rule (section 4) | `output.factors.thrown`: consumables only | ×1 | **×0.7** |

**One constant per system, no ladder** (a call made for Leon, item 1712): the all-in measure averages on its ceiling over levels 1, 5, 10 and 20 within ±12%, and no level is more than 25% off. All in is a little over early and a little under late, because the all-in build's head start is accuracy, which the normal build catches by level 13. The ladder the proposal preferred (class rank III and the Mastered perk carrying the last 25%) needs those moves designed and measured first (PATCH-TALLY 10, row 5).

### 3. Flat things grow with level

A grenade, a blast's splash, a charge, a trap, a hazard, a barrel, and the ticks of Bleeding, Burning and Corroded take a Level term (effects/mending.ts `flatLevelOf`):
1. **Made by a character:** its level through the flat profile (the deal column).
2. **Made by an enemy or a companion:** its own tier and level (`lvlDmg`, rules 1.15), as its weapon. An enemy's splash was already scaled so; it is now scaled in that one place.
3. **Made by nobody** (a hazard, a map trap, a barrel nobody set off, a failed approach): the fight's level through the enemy table's damage column, as enemies grow.
4. A derived weapon hit (the carried round, the wrench) already carries its weapon's terms and takes none.

### 4. Many targets, control, and the budget rule

1. **The cluster** (measured: the reference squad's fights against a standard group, sampled from round 2 on): a shape aimed at one enemy catches on average **2.4** enemies at radius 1, **2.8** at radius 2, **2.95** at radius 3; a chain always finds its second (2.0).
2. **The per-extra-target rule:** an area is worth its single-target allowance **plus half of it for each extra target** it is expected to catch (`balance.yardsticks.area.extra_target_share` 0.5). So a radius-1 shape may deal each target up to 1.7 ÷ 2.4 = 0.71 of the single-target number, a radius-2 shape 1.9 ÷ 2.8 = 0.68. Sigil SPREAD (×0.6) and the Outburst's Wave, Burst and Aura (×0.7, 0.7, 0.6) are inside it; CHAIN (a second target at ×0.75: 1.75 against 1.5) is 17% over and was not changed (item 1716).
3. **A frag at 40** on the measured cluster was 1.5 times the budget rule's allowance for 2 AP of the plain tier with the session-supply and credits allowance; the thrown factor brings it to 28.
4. **Control:** a whole Soldier turn denied is worth **one rifle-turn** (100%); one AP off it a sixth; an Elite ×1.4, a Boss ×3 and never a whole turn; never the same enemy two rounds running (the Cut Short rule, for everything). A condition is worth the share of the enemy's turn it removes × its rounds × the chance it lands (`balance.yardsticks.control`; the table is in the contract).
5. **Damage over time** counts in full for 2 rounds and ×0.75 for longer.

### 5. What changed besides numbers

1. Rarity's numbers moved from `character.ts` into `data/rules.json rarity` (the table in Weapons v2, Rarity, now reads: Masterwork **+2 accuracy, +50% durability, +1 mod slot**; the +10% damage is gone).
2. The enemy AI's estimate of a field's bite (ai-sigil.ts `biteOf`) counts the owner's Line multiplier and Level term, as the engine deals it; it left the Line out, so a field that kills was read as one that nearly does.
3. The balance contract and its guard (`npm run check`).

## Rules revision 1.27 (the heal re-fit): a healer's turn is worth two Soldier-turns, and the untrained have a floor

> **Superseded by rules 1.36** (heals and shields in percent of HP): the 2.0 Soldier-turn ceiling, its Stat floor's role as the floor (the gate is the floor now; the profiles' `floor` is kept and never binds) and the Hymn heal cap of 250 are replaced by the percent lines.


Built on 12 Nov 2026 from Leon's report on live 0.23.0 ("a recruit at level 0 soul skill and a fully pumped soul mend heals for 6, his HP is 125, we might have over-nerfed the healing") and the lead's ruling on it. It overrides the healer's ceiling of rules 1.26 (section 2, "A healer's turn"), the bands of rules 1.20 (section 2) and the medic's bands of rules 1.23 wherever they state a size. Every number below is **PROVISIONAL** (items 1730 to 1741).

### 1. Why it was too low

1. **A rifle turn removes about a whole Soldier, a heal does not.** Killing a Soldier cancels its damage for the rest of the fight; healing 1.25 Soldier-turns a turn only undoes one turn of it. At 1.25 healing lost to shooting in every case but saving someone about to drop. Leon had already ruled on the other side of it: "if a tank is unkillable because a healer is healing them dedicatedly, let them have it" (the enemies hunt the healer instead: rules 1.23 and 1.25).
2. **The untrained.** A caster with no points in the healing skill heals with a Stat term of 1 against 1.42 for a normal share (4 and 4) and 1.78 all in (7 and 7). On one Stat term that is 70% of a normal share; a Sigil boon multiplies two (its own landed Stat and Healing given), so a caster with nothing in either lands at about half.

### 2. The ruling

1. **A healer's turn, all in, is worth 2.0 Soldier-turns** (it was 1.25); a normal share 1.6 (the ratio of 1.25 stays). `data/rules.json balance.ceilings.healer_turn.allin` **200**.
2. **Every heal and every shield** that goes through the heal and shield profiles was scaled by 2.0 ÷ 1.25 = **×1.6** by its dial (`output.profiles`) and re-measured (`test/balance/heal-measure.ts`); each dial was trimmed so its system's all-in average over levels 1, 5, 10 and 20 sits on 200, each level within the contract's ±25%:

| Dial | Was | ×1.6 | Now | What it moves | All in, levels 1 / 5 / 10 / 20 (percent of a Soldier-turn) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `healing.k` (Healing given) | 0.87 | 1.392 | **1.392** | the Outburst's Buff heal and Love, the medic's kit, every class heal or shield that scales with Healing given, and (as its second Stat term) a Sigil boon | the Soul healer's steady turn: 234 / 211 / 195 / 158 (average 200; it was 146 / 132 / 122 / 99) |
| `mend.k` | 0.87 | 1.392 | **1.392** | an item's heal or shield through the `mend` op | follows `healing.k` (the same pair) |
| `soul_mend.k` | 0.81 | 1.296 | **1.296** | the Soul shields (Inverse, Shell) | ×1.6, as the Soul heal |
| `sigil_mend.k` | 1.2 | 1.92 | **1.17** | MEND and WARD | MEND · CONDENSE · SEEK (about 5.5 AP, one turn): 235 / 212 / 196 / 158 (average 200; it was 151 / 136 / 125 / 101). At 1.92 it was 386 / 348 / 321 / 259: a boon also multiplies by Healing given, so `healing.k` already carried the ×1.6 into it |
| `blessing_mend.k` | 0.956 | 1.53 | **1.44** (capped) | every prayer heal and shield, and Mother Ember's intervention | a Hymn turn's healing (Warm Hands and Health): 249 / 224 / 208 / 168 (it was 166 / 149 / 138 / 111). At ×1.6 it was 265 at level 1, past the cap of 2.5 Soldier-turns: capped there (×1.51) |

3. **Faith's heal dial is live now.** A prayer's Stat is Blessing power (the `blessing` profile, which is also its damage). A prayer heal or shield, and Mother Ember's intervention, multiply by `blessing_mend.k ÷ blessing.k` (faith.ts `mendDial`), so one number moves Faith's healing and nothing of its damage. Before this revision `blessing_mend.k` was read by nothing.
4. **The medic's kit** (Triage, a stim, Stim Throw, Rally, a Field Repair on an ally) is base × Healing given × the level factor, so it rose ×1.6 through `healing.k`; its bases (`mending.medic`: Triage 5, a dose 6, Rally 6, Field Repair 3 a point) did not move. In a medic's hands Triage is now 45 to 51% of a Soldier-turn for 2 AP (28 to 32% under rules 1.26), a dose 53 to 63% for 1 AP; a dose in anyone's hands 25 to 43%.
5. **A floor for the untrained.** Each heal and shield profile (`healing`, `mend`, `sigil_mend`, `soul_mend`, `blessing_mend`) has `floor` **0.5**: its Stat term is never under half of a normal share's, a normal share being `output.floor_reference` (4 in each Attribute and Skill of the pair). It is in the formula's one place (`effects/output.ts statTerm`), on the landed heal profiles only; no damage profile has one. **With today's slopes it binds nowhere** (no points is 70% of a normal share on every Stat term); it holds the rule if a slope is raised or a term added.
6. **Enemy healers do not change:** an enemy caster heals with its own bases (`heal_enemy`, `shield_enemy`) and a Healing given of 1; nothing of theirs reads these dials.

### 3. The case Leon reported

A Recruit (the Proving Ground's Sharpshooter: Insight 1, no Soul skill) releasing the Mend design at stage 4 (×1.6) on an ally, through the reducer:

| Level | 1 | 5 | 10 | 20 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before (rules 1.26) | 9 | 10 | 12 | 17 |
| Now | **15** | **17** | **19** | **28** |

Before, the same Mend at stage 1 (×1.0) healed 6 at level 1: the number Leon saw. Now it is 9.

The Soul healer's steady turn (stage 4 with Rage, Love and two plain Pumps), HP healed and Soldier-turns:

| Level | 1 | 5 | 10 | 20 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Normal share, before → now | 21 (1.12) → **33 (1.79)** | 28 (1.15) → **44 (1.85)** | 38 (1.12) → **61 (1.79)** | 59 (0.99) → **95 (1.58)** |
| All in, before → now | 27 (1.46) → **43 (2.34)** | 32 (1.32) → **51 (2.11)** | 42 (1.22) → **67 (1.95)** | 59 (0.99) → **95 (1.58)** |

### 4. The tank, dedicated-healed

The pair of rules 1.23 (the tank in front, a Soul healer behind it healing every turn; 10 fights a cell, ten rounds at most), with the healer **all in**: rounds before the first Down, before → now. Under two Soldiers: 10 → 10, 10 → 10, 10 → 10, 6.8 → 7.1 (levels 1, 6, 12, 20). Under three: 4.8 → 5.3, 8.8 → 8.0, 9.1 → 9.1, 2.9 → 3.6. The one who drops first is mostly the healer, as the doctrine intends; the tank is dropped first in 10 to 80% of the fights under three (most at level 12). With a normal-share healer the pair under three Soldiers lasts 5.0 → 5.6, 8.4 → 9.0, 7.9 → 9.8, 8.7 → 9.7 rounds, and nobody is Down after ten rounds in 70 to 80% of the fights from level 6 (30 to 40% before). "Unkillable while dedicated-healed" is closer than it was, and allowed (Leon); not tuned against.

### 5. What it leaves open

1. The guards' bands for the Whisper and the Hymn as damage did not move (no damage number moved).
2. The normal share does not hold the ratio of 1.25 at level 20 (it catches all in by level 13, as every system does: rules 1.26 section 2).
3. The all-in Soul healer of the simulator heals 2 to 8 times a fight under fire against 8 to 10 for the normal share (its policy runs short of MP or reach under fire); not investigated here.

## Rules revision 1.28: the engine's general primitives (Classes 3.0, step 1)

Built on 13 Nov 2026 for Class Roster Revision 4 ("Classes 3.0"; `docs/design/rev4-primitives.md`). It overrides every body
line on reactions and on Suppressed that says otherwise (rules 1.3 "Reactions", the condition table, items 83 and 89).

### 1. Two rules (Leon, 13 Nov 2026)

1. **A reaction never triggers a reaction.** While a reaction resolves, no other reaction can be made by anyone: no
   Riposte of a Riposte, no Parry or Riposte of an opportunity attack's blow, no Interpose of an Overwatch shot; a
   reaction's move (Duck and Roll's step) draws no opportunity attack and sets off no held shot.
2. **Suppressed never blocks a protective reaction.** Every reaction is one of three kinds: it **attacks** (an
   opportunity attack, a held shot of any kind, Riposte, Keep Back, Catch, Dance of Iron, Heart Overwatch, a Call made
   as a reaction), it **moves** you (Duck and Roll, a dive clear) or it **protects** (Parry, Shield Wall, Interpose, Shrug
   It Off, Anchor, a Heartbinder's Share). The condition Suppressed and Pressure's Suppressed state (rules 1.12) are one
   rule: they forbid attacking and moving reactions and never protective ones. Stunned, Downed and Dread underfoot still
   leave no reaction at all.

Also, with them: **one event, one reaction a unit** (a unit with two reactions answers a single attack, step or hit
once); the round's count is the counters' cell of scope `reaction` (on the area map it lives in the story, so a unit
rebuilt there gets no fresh reaction each action).

### 2. The primitives (no rule changes)

The engine gained, generally and once, what the Revision 4 systems will stand on; none of it changes play. **acted**,
a trigger after a unit's own action succeeds (Analyze fires its own); **number blocks** (`{base, per: [{of, value}],
min, max}`) for any numeric field of an item op, counting `res:`, `event:`, `self:`, `actor:` and `target:` sources,
and `"all"` / `"zero"` for a resource; **react()**, the one door of every reaction (above); **conditions are items**
(a condition row's triggered effects run for its bearer, its stats answer); the unit set **targets** on any op; the
**sight words** seen, unseen, in view, out of view (`self_sight`, `actor_sight`, `target_sight`, stat `always_seen`,
a unit's `eyes`); and the closed-list rows `spot`, `by_cover`, `patron`, `via`, `nonlethal`, `heal_kind` and the
resource rows (Pressure, MP). How each is written: `docs/design/handoffs/classes-3.0-step-1a.md`. Items 1750 to 1756.

### 3. Three rulings on the reaction kinds (the lead, 13 Nov 2026, on step 1a's review; Leon can reverse)

1. **An Order is the ordered ally's reaction.** What the ally does on an Order (stand, reload, pick up, move) is that
   ally's reaction, of kind move: being a reaction, it provokes nothing (its move draws no opportunity attack and sets
   off no held shot). An Order made itself as a reaction spends the ally's reaction all the same.
2. **Anchor's strike is an attack.** The opportunity attack Anchor makes on a Disengaging enemy is an attacking
   reaction: Suppressed stops it. (Anchor's refusal to be moved is not a reaction.)
3. **Drink It In and a helping Call are protective.** They help an ally and move or hurt nobody, so Suppressed does not
   stop them. **A Call that harms or hinders an enemy is never a reaction** (the lead's ruling at the step's integration,
   13 Nov 2026): it is made on your own turn only (Spot, Threaten, Taunt); from 9 points only a helping Call can be made
   as a reaction.

With them, one key names every answer to a step of a walk (an opportunity attack, Overwatch, a held Watch, Heart
Overwatch, Anchor): a unit with two reactions answers one step once, whichever reaction it makes; the same tiles walked
again are another step.

### 4. The primitives of step 1b (no rule changes)

The engine also gained: **one hook for every roll to hit** (a weapon attack's, a Sigil's and an Outburst's ask the same
hook, so an item that changes "a roll to hit this target" reaches all three; Leon, 13 Nov 2026); **door verbs** (an
item of kind `verb` held by every sheet that meets its `requires`; its action's `res`, `if`, `reach`, `pick`, `limit` and
`prayer`, a Whisper or a Hymn prayed as one of the patron's own); **zones from data** (a `zone` op, the predicates
`self_in_zone` and `target_in_zone`, a zone's `pool`); **shield layers** (a shield on a named layer beside the base
shield, spent first, the newest first, at most `holders` units carrying one giver's); **data toggles** (an item's flag on
an existing action, its effects running while it is on); **ties** (an edge of a kind between two units, a cap per
holder, the end rules from_down, to_down, to_dead, unseen_round and combat_end); **owned units** (a unit one unit owns:
the tie `owned` and its block's turn, eyes, upkeep, cover and lure; the drone and the beast are tied to their owner as a
fight starts, their turn unchanged); **delay** on any op; the number source `ties:`; the predicates `self_holds` and
`self_lacks_gear` (the one test of a focus in hand); `redirect` and its `split`; the standing aura (a stat answered for
every unit near its holder); `via` on a condition; the witness filter; and the percent gate and cap of a heal or a
shield (`heal-shield-percent-spec.md`), with no number set. How each is written:
`docs/design/handoffs/classes-3.0-step-1b.md`. Items 1762 to 1767.

### 5. Completed at the step's integration (the lead's rulings, 13 Nov 2026; no rule of play changes)

1. **A unit with no turn of its own.** An owned unit whose block says its turn is its owner's is never in the turn
   order: on its owner's turn its verbs (a move, its weapon's plain attacks, as its block lists them) are its owner's
   actions, made with the owned unit and paid from its owner's AP. One whose turn is automatic acts once at the start of
   its owner's turn, at the target its block names (the nearest enemy or the most hurt), paid the same way.
2. **One tie for every owned unit.** A drone, a beast and a Figment are all tied to their owner by the one tie `owned`;
   what each is (a companion, a figment) is written on the unit, and a rule that treats them differently reads that.
3. **A Call that harms or hinders an enemy is never a reaction** (section 3, rule 3, as amended).
4. **The four rows left from the batch:** a heal or shield of a kind can be multiplied by an item (`mend_mult`: Bonds'
   ×1.2 through a Bond); an item that cancels a condition on an ally can take that condition itself (`incoming`: Take
   the Weight); an intervention can leave Witnessed on (a stat: the Chaplain); and the condition **Read**: its source's
   side sees what the bearer means to do on its next turn until that turn ends. Items 1768 and 1769.

## Rules revision 1.29: Classes 3.0, the nine base classes renamed (Classes 3.0, steps 2 and 4)

Built on 13 Nov 2026 for Class Roster Revision 4 (`docs/design/rev4-moves-and-rename.md` sections 1, 3 and 5). It
overrides every body line that names a base class by its old name.

### 1. The rename (names only; no rule changes)

| Class id (unchanged) | Was (Revision 3) | Now (Classes 3.0) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `defender` | Defender | **Bulwark** |
| `fighter` | Fighter | **Breaker** |
| `marksman` | Marksman | **Skirmisher** |
| `infiltrator` | Infiltrator | **Operative** |
| `mage` | Mage | **Sigilist** |
| `trickster` | Trickster | **Rigger** |
| `bard` | Bard | **Mender** |
| `channeler` | Channeler | Channeler (unchanged) |
| `guardian` | Guardian | **Chaplain** |

Only the display name changes (`data/classes.json` `base[].name`, and the Revision 2 shells' names). The ids, every
move key (`class:<origin>.<moveId>`), the saved `classId` and `classRev` (3) are as they were, so a save or a
character made before the rename loads with the same class and the same moves, and shows the new name. Advanced
classes keep their own names ("Circuit Mage" is an advanced class, not the Sigilist). The archetype families
(Frontline, Shadows, Sigil casters…) are playstyles and keep their names. **Three archetype presets had a new class's
name** (an archetype may not share a class's name: the validator's rule), so they show new names; their ids, portraits
and points are unchanged, and an archetype is never saved: Bulwark → **Holdfast** (`bulwark`), Sigilist →
**Glyphwright** (`sigilist`), Mender → **Empath** (`mender`) *(Suggested)*. Three emblems are redrawn (Rigger: a
wrench crossed with a spark; Mender: two hands around a plus; Chaplain: a dome under a flame); the other six keep
theirs. Items 1757 and 1758.

### 2. The classes that keep their mechanic, made a little better (PROVISIONAL)

| Class | Change | Number |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Bulwark** | A fight starts with Guard (the cap stays 5). | 1 Guard |
| **Breaker** | Once a turn, your first hit on a **Shaken** or **Frightened** (Fear) enemy, with **any** weapon, on your own turn, gives Momentum, on top of what the hit itself gives (a melee hit's 1). The cap stays 5. Riposte is unchanged here (the reaction rule's step folds it into the Answer). | 1 Momentum, once a turn |
| **Sigilist** | Unchanged in this step. Its one Revision 4 change (BLIND, SLOW and MUDDLE back to the common word list, MUDDLE's −1 charge gone) is the Rigger's move leaving the class: built with the Rigger. | |
| **Channeler** | Unchanged. | |

Both changes are item ops in data (`data/classes.json`): the Bulwark's on Brace (`{op: resource, when: combat_start,
resource: guard, value: 1}`), the Breaker's on Lunge (`{op: resource, when: hit, resource: momentum, value: 1, if:
{own_turn, hostile, target_has: [shaken, fear]}, limit: {per: per_turn, n: 1}}`). Each class gets its rank I moves at
level 3, so the change comes with the class; it sits on a rank I move until the engine has a base class's own effects
block (the design's "class `effects`"), then moves there unchanged. Items 1759 and 1760.

### 3. Base classes are weapon-neutral (Leon, 13 Nov 2026): the guard

No Bulwark, Breaker, Sigilist or Channeler move is locked to a weapon family (`docs/design/rev4-weapon-neutral-audit.md`
sections 3.1, 3.2, 3.5, 3.8): Lunge, Riposte and Finisher ask for a melee weapon (or fists) because Momentum is
melee's meter, and Anchor's opportunity attack is a melee blow because every opportunity attack is. The guard
`packages/engine/test/class-weapon-neutral.test.ts` checks every base-class move's data, text and handler; the moves
still locked (Fire Discipline, Speed Loader, Special Ammo, Killzone, Called Shot, Toxin, Judgement) are on its PENDING
list, which the Skirmisher's, Shadow's and the Chaplain's steps empty. Item 1761.
## Rules revision 1.30: reactions made real, and the Skirmisher (Classes 3.0, step 3)

Built on 13 Nov 2026 from `docs/design/reactions-spec.md` (binding) and `docs/design/rev4-weapon-neutral-audit.md` 4.1.
It overrides every body line on reactions and on the Marksman's moves that says otherwise (rules 1.3 "Reactions", the
class table of rules 1.10, items 89 and 1750 to 1756 where they differ). The class id stays `marksman`; its display name
is the rename step's. Every number here is PROVISIONAL (items 1800 to 1813).

### 1. The reaction rule, complete

1. **Everyone has one reaction a round** (`rules.json combat.reactions.per_round`, 1); a new round gives it back.
   Everything a unit does outside its own turn spends one.
2. **A reaction never triggers a reaction**, and **one event, one reaction a unit** (rules 1.28, unchanged).
3. **More only from:** Reflex (the Skirmisher: two), an item that says so (Before the Blink: one more), a Call that
   gives one (Cue: exactly one, before the giver's next turn), or a Many Hands donor's (spent on the donor).
4. **A reaction that attacks is a plain attack** (the weapon's plain shot or blow), unless its own text gives it
   something (Riposte's Edge or Point +2, the Breaker's Counter; Overwatch's +2 when Precise; Killzone's +2).
5. **Held fire:** a held Burst fires its rounds on one reaction. **Killzone** holds two attacks and **spends both of
   the Skirmisher's reactions** on the first one it fires; with one reaction left, only one fires.
6. **Suppressed** forbids attacking and moving reactions, never protective ones (rules 1.28); **forced movement**
   provokes nothing (`rules.json forced_movement`).
7. **Keep one for a held shot** (on by default): a unit with two or more reactions that holds a shot (Overwatch, a
   Watch, Killzone, a held Outburst's watch) never spends its last reaction on anything that fires by itself (an
   opportunity attack, an Answer, Duck and Roll, an item's reaction): the held shot keeps it.
8. **The dial** `rules.json combat.reactions.second_hit` (0): a to-hit step on the attack of a unit's second reaction
   in a round, defined and unused (moved only if the measured Skirmisher passes its line by more than 12%).

### 2. The Skirmisher (`marksman`; Agility): the class

**At class gain, Reflex:** two reactions a round (stat `reactions` +1). **Weapon-neutral** (Leon, 13 Nov 2026): every
move works with whatever the Skirmisher attacks with; only Heat stays the gun's.

| Rank | Move | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| I | **Fire Discipline** | Aimed attacks have +1 to hit, and with a weapon that has Heat they add none. Once a turn, on your turn, a weapon technique that costs 3 AP or more costs 1 AP less (a Burst 2, a Mag Dump, a dear blow: any weapon). The free techniques everyone has (a shot, an Aimed shot, a blow) are never cheaper (item 1813). |
| I | **Speed Loader** | Your first main-hand reload, draw, swap or pick-up each turn costs 1 AP less (at least 1). |
| II | **Duck and Roll** | Unchanged (reaction, kind move). |
| II | **Special Ammo** | One load each of armour-piercing, hollow-point and incendiary a rest, on any weapon: a magazine for a gun, a quiver of 12 for a bow (filled before the fight), and for a blade, a fist or a thrown blade a load that lasts 12 attacks or the fight. Loading is your reload's AP; 1 AP for a weapon that never reloads. Never a consumable (a grenade is its own payload). The rounds' effects are `rules.json ammo_types`. |
| III | **Killzone** | Hold two attacks with any weapon, for twice the attack's AP: one at each of the first two different enemies that move into your line (a gun, a bow) or your reach (a melee weapon), +2 to hit each. It spends both your reactions; with one left, only one fires. |
| III | **Run and Gun** (new) | Once a turn, after you attack, your next move of up to 2 tiles costs no AP and draws no opportunity attack, and your next hit this turn, with any weapon, adds 1 more Pressure. |

**Called Shot leaves the class** (to the Operative, Classes 3.0 step 4); its key `gunslinger.called_shot` stays.

### 3. Riposte: the two become one

The Breaker's class Riposte and the technique Riposte are one Answer and one reaction. The class move gives the
Breaker the Answer with any melee weapon and two riders on it: it costs 1 Momentum, and it adds the Breaker's Counter
bonus to hit. With no Momentum the Breaker does not Riposte (even with a weapon that lends the technique). The
technique's own policy (the character's Answers) is the only on/off.

### 4. The perk Bulwark is renamed Stonewall

The Durability perk `bulwark` (allies directly behind you take less from ranged attacks) shared its name with the class
the Defender became (rules 1.29), so it is renamed **Stonewall** *(Suggested)*: display name only; the id `bulwark`, its
icon (`art/icons/perks/bulwark.png`), its numbers and a saved character's perk are unchanged. "Rampart" was the first
choice and was not used: the RAISE Grand form is "Ramparts". `tools/validate.py` now refuses a perk named as a class,
as it already refused an archetype. Item 1812.

## Rules revision 1.31: the Chaplain, and prayer from Faith 1 (Classes 3.0, step 5)

Built on 13 Nov 2026 from `docs/design/chaplain-spec.md` (binding; its "Settled" notes override its body), the Settled
blocks of `docs/design/class-roster-rev4-proposal.md` section 8 and `docs/design/rev4-weapon-neutral-audit.md` 4.7. It
overrides every body line on who may pray (rules 1.6: "praying at all needs Faith 3"), on the Guardian's moves (the
class table of rules 1.10 and rules 1.29), on Will Shield, Command, Sanctuary and Judgement, where they differ. The class
id stays `guardian`; its display name is the Chaplain (rules 1.29). Every number here is PROVISIONAL (items 1900 to 1949).

### 1. Prayer opens at Faith 1 (Leon, 13 Nov 2026)

1. **Whispers from Faith 1** (`patrons.json prayer.whisper.faith_min`, 1; `prayer.faith_min`, the least of the two):
   one Whisper a turn, 1 AP, the Faithful to their patron and an Atheist by dice against 12, as before.
2. **Hymns from Faith 3** (`prayer.hymn.faith_min`, 3), as built; Witnessed at Faith 5 and the Miracle at Faith 7 and
   Devotion 10 unchanged. A Whisper's size grows with Faith through Blessing power, so a Faith 1 Whisper is small.
3. The refusals: "Praying needs Faith 1." (a Whisper), "A Hymn needs Faith 3." (a Hymn, a door verb that is a Hymn,
   Blessed Arms' story blessing), "A Miracle needs Faith 7.". The Belief step's note reads both thresholds from the engine.

### 2. The Chaplain's moves (`classes.json` the `guardian` block; `move_pool` `guardian.sanctuary`)

| Rank | Key | Move | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| I | `guardian.ward` | **Ward** | A Whisper only the Chaplain can say; it **uses the turn's one Whisper** (1 AP; the Atheist's roll). An ally in sight, never yourself, gains a shield of **10 × Blessing power** (`amounts.ward`, profile `blessing_mend`: Blessing power × the prayer heal dial × the level's growth) for the fight, on its own layer `ward` (spent before any other shield; every other shield is the base layer, where the larger stands). **At most 2 allies** carry your Ward (a third ends the oldest); a Ward on an ally who has one tops it up, never doubles. |
| I | `guardian.smite` | **Smite** | Once a turn, on your own turn, when an attack with your weapon (any: a shot, a strike, a throw, two weapons, a focus's attack; trigger `hit`) hits an enemy that still stands, the patron also deals **20 × Blessing power Soul** (`amounts.smite`, Rebuke's base; no roll, armour does not lower it). Not multiplied by the technique, a critical, Verdict or ammunition (it is an item's damage, not the attack's). A hit that kills leaves it for a later hit that turn; never on another's turn (a reaction, an opportunity attack). It is a prayer: `via: faith` (a kill by prayer for the No Magic but Theirs vow), Old Overcast's is lightning (`amounts.smite_storm`, element lightning: the storm tag); not a Whisper and uses no prayer limit. The Toll-Keeper's and the Matchmaker's (taboo `kill`) are `nonlethal`: a Smite that would take the last HP subdues. An Atheist rolls the Whisper's TN on each hit it would ride (predicate `answered`); a miss leaves it unspent. It needs the prayer door open (Faith 1, not Silenced). |
| II | `lumeri_templar.under_the_eye` | Under the Eye | As built (allies within 3 get +2 to hit while you are Witnessed; any weapon). |
| II | `lumeri_templar.blessed_shells` | **Blessed Arms** *(Suggested; was Blessed Shells)* | As built, any weapon: a landed Hymn loads into your weapon (a round, an arrow, an edge, a thrown blade); the next hit releases it; a Smite may ride the same hit. Tag `guns` → `weapon`; the story action is "Bless your weapon". |
| III | `guardian.sanctuary` | **Sanctuary** | A Hymn only the Chaplain can say (3 AP; it starts the one Hymn wait: no patron Hymn until it ends; tier 1 for the Faithful's overreach; the Atheist's Hymn I roll). A tile in sight within 6 (`reach.tile`): allies on its 3×3, you included, take half damage (rounded up) until the start of your next turn; it prevents at most **11 × Blessing power** (`amounts.sanctuary_cap`, profile `blessing_mend`, rounded) in all, then ends. Your own Strain burn is not halved. An answered Sanctuary makes the Faithful Witnessed (Faith 5). No MP, no Strain. |
| III | `lumeri_templar.judgement` | **Verdict** *(Suggested; was Judgement; key kept)* | As built (4 AP, 10 Devotion XP, once a fight, × (1 + Blessing power)), with **any weapon**: the weapon's plain attack (a strike if it is a melee weapon, a throw if it is a thrown one, else a shot); never a Burst, an Aimed shot or a technique. The gate "a melee weapon or a scattergun" is gone. |
| gain | `guardian.at_your_side` | **The Patron at Your Side** | Section 3. |

**Removed:** Will Shield (`guardian.will_shield`, replaced by Ward), Command (out: an order is Authority's Call), the old
Sanctuary's MP, Strain, once a scene and Soul cast (its handler; its story half is now a Narrator action, no MP).
**No MP and no Strain:** no Chaplain move costs MP, Strain, cores or ammunition of its own; the class's `resources` are
`["devotion"]`. Verdict keeps its Devotion XP cost.

### 3. The patron at its side (the presence)

1. **Judged** (`conditions.json`, a state, 1 round, no save): an enemy the Chaplain's weapon hits on its own turn. Its
   source is the Chaplain: it is how "where the weapon struck" is known.
2. **The presence:** while a Faithful Chaplain is Witnessed, its patron stands on its tile as a presence (stat
   `patron_presence`, answered by the class gain): not a unit, never targeted, blocks nothing, sees nothing, moves with
   it. It ends when Witnessed ends. Downed: it stays (dimmed); dead: it ends.
3. **The first intervention of a fight does not end Witnessed** (stat `intervention_keeps_witnessed` 1: the first that
   many interventions keep it); the second (Devotion 7) ends it. The count is the door's (once, twice from Devotion 7);
   the presence never adds an intervention.
4. **Each patron's intervention reaches further** (`patrons.json` each patron's `intervention.presence`):

| Patron | The door's | With the presence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Holy Father Nerukhan | an enemy harms the helpless | also when an enemy the Chaplain has Judged damages an ally to a quarter of their HP or less (`judged_harms_below` 0.25) |
| The Quartermaster | your reload is free | also an ally's reload within 1 tile (`ally_within` 1) |
| The Laughing Mask | an enemy misses you: Prone | also a miss on an ally within 1 |
| The Toll-Keeper | an ally stays at 1 HP | the ally kept up also gains your Ward (`ward`: the Chaplain's Ward item) |
| Mother Ember | an ally below a quarter heals | below half instead (`below` 0.5; the door's quarter is `intervention.below`) |
| Old Overcast | your kill: lightning on the nearest other enemy | on a Judged enemy of yours first (`judged_first`) |
| The Matchmaker | an ally next to you is hit: half moves to you | an ally within 2 |
| The Counting Weaver | an enemy crits you: a normal hit | also a crit on an ally within 1 |

### 4. What the engine gained (general, for the next system too)

- A prayer's own effects (a `grant_action` with `prayer`, on any item, not only a door verb) run only when the patron
  answers; the item's triggered effects stay with their triggers.
- `reach.tile` (a door verb aimed at a tile within `tiles`, in sight when `sight`).
- The `zone` op's `pool` may name the item's amount block (worked out when the zone is laid, rounded).
- Predicates `not_patron` (words) and `answered` (a prayer riding an event: the Faithful always, an Atheist rolls the
  Whisper's TN; rolled last). The `say` placeholder `{patron}`; the `deal` op hands what reached the target to `{then}`.
- An amount block's `element` (the damage's element tag when it is not its type).
- Stat `patron_presence`.

### 5. The balance line

The Chaplain's own line is **125% of a rifle-turn all in** (`rules.json balance.ceilings.chaplain_turn`; Leon). The
measured table is in `docs/design/handoffs/classes-3.0-step-5.md`. Shield sizes (Ward 10, Sanctuary's 11) are step 7b's
to re-fit through `amounts.ward.base` and `amounts.sanctuary_cap.base` (Faith's shield is to be the strongest: Leon).

## Rules revision 1.32: Shadow and the Operative (Classes 3.0, step 6)

Built on 13 Nov 2026 from `docs/design/shadow-spec.md` (binding; its "Settled" notes override its body) and
`docs/design/rev4-weapon-neutral-audit.md` 4.4. It overrides every body line on the Ambush multiplier, Ingenuity's
per-point line and unlocks, and the Infiltrator's moves that says otherwise (rules 1.3 "combat Hidden", the class table
of rules 1.10, rules 1.29's Operative). The class id stays `infiltrator`, its display name the Operative. Every number
here is PROVISIONAL (items 1950 to 1969).

### 1. Sight, in the engine's words

**Hidden** is the flag (`u.hidden`; the condition row `hidden`). **In view**: some living, standing enemy's eyes reach
your tile, Hidden or not. **Seen**: not Hidden and in view. **Can't see you** (a target): its eyes don't reach your
tile, or you are Hidden. Data reads these through the sight words (`self_sight`, `actor_sight`, `target_sight`) and
`target_sees_self` (false while you are Hidden). A Silent weapon attacks without ending Hidden, as before.

### 2. The door: the Shadow meter (anyone with Ingenuity)

1. **The meter** (`res.shadow`, `data/rules.json shadow`): cap 1 at Ingenuity 1, 2 at 5, 3 at 7 (`cap_by_points`). It
   starts each fight at 0 and is 0 when you go Down and when the fight ends. Built like Guard: a pool for anyone with
   the skill. Item 1950.
2. **Gains** (each +1; the door item, `skills.json ingenuity.1`): (a) your turn ends Hidden and you made no attack this
   turn (an attack rolled marks the turn: a hit, a miss or a shot cover stops); (b) once a turn, a move of your own
   (a move or a Sprint, never a push) that starts and ends next to cover, made Hidden and ending out of view; (c) your
   hit drops an enemy and, after the attack, you are not Seen. **At most 2 a turn** from (a) to (c) together
   (`door_gains_per_turn`); a gain at the cap is lost. Item 1951.
3. **Losses:** at the start of each of your turns, −1 while you are Seen; a Break spends it all; Fade spends 2. Item 1952.
4. **The Break** (Ingenuity 1): a toggle on any weapon attack or weapon technique of yours (a shot, an Aimed Shot, a
   Burst, a melee technique, a throw), never a spell, prayer, Call or reaction. It needs Hidden and 1 Shadow. Every roll
   of that one action takes **one** multiplier `shadow` = 1 + **0.15 a point spent** (`per_point`) + **0.5 on a fresh
   ambush** (`ambush_bonus`: the first attack of a Hidden entry) + **0.15 against an enemy you Marked**
   (`marked_bonus`). It stands in place of the Ambush multiplier (the two never multiply). When the action ends the
   Shadow is spent and you are revealed, even with a Silent weapon. The Elite and Boss guard holds every roll of it. Item 1953.
5. **The Ambush multiplier is a flat ×1.5** (1 + `ambush_bonus`): Ingenuity's +5% a point is gone. Crits on 19-20 come
   with the ambush, as before. Item 1954.
6. **A silent attack from Hidden** lets its target, if it is still up and its eyes reach your tile, roll to spot you at
   once (the spotting roll, for that one looker; no reaction spent). Item 1955.

### 3. The verbs (`data/shadow.json`; door verbs, anyone whose Ingenuity reaches them)

Every verb but Lift needs you Hidden; "unseen" means the target can't see you. Saves are against 12 + your Ingenuity
strength. Built:

| Verb | Opens | Cost | Does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lift | 3 | 2 AP | an adjacent enemy's grenade, else a spare magazine, goes into the pile on your tile; if it can see you, a Body save keeps it |
| Read Intent | 3 | 1 AP | an unseen enemy within 8 is Read: your side sees its next action until its turn ends |
| Cut the Strap | 3 | 1 AP, 1 Shadow | an adjacent unseen enemy is Disarmed (its save) |
| Fade | 5 | 2 AP, 2 Shadow | even while Seen: step to the nearest tile next to cover within your Movement (one out of view first) and become Hidden (a new entry). Not while Marked |
| Open Seam | 5 | 1 AP, 1 Shadow | an unseen enemy within 8 is **Exposed** (Defense −2, 1 round) |
| Foul the Action | 5 | 1 AP, 1 Shadow | an adjacent unseen enemy's weapon is Lowered (its save) |
| Still Breath | 5 | passive | spot rolls against you are −2 while you stand next to cover |
| Timing | 7 | 1 AP, 1 Shadow | an unseen enemy within 8 is **Off Balance** (−1 AP on its next turn); never the same enemy two rounds running |
| Plant | 7 | 2 AP, 1 Shadow | an adjacent unseen enemy is Marked by you |
| Disable | 7 | 2 AP, 1 Shadow | an adjacent machine, robot, turret or drone is Stunned 1 round (its save) |
| Hijack | 9 | 2 AP, 2 Shadow | an adjacent machine, robot, turret or drone is Puppeted 1 round (its save) |
| Decoy | 3 | 1 AP, 1 Shadow | a sound on a tile within 5: every other side now places you there (its last-seen tile of you: its searchers go there). Item 1970 |
| Close Quarters | 3 | passive | an enemy next to you while you are Hidden rolls to spot you at +4 instead of finding you outright. Item 1971 |
| Vault | 5 | 1 AP | cross one tile of half cover, a barricade or a hole to the free tile beyond it (two tiles away, in a straight line). Item 1972 |
| Pick | 5 | 1 AP | a door next to you, no check: locked or closed, it opens; open, it closes and locks. Item 1973 |
| Douse | 5 | 1 AP | a lamp within 2 goes out (its HP to 0). Item 1973 |
| Shadow Run | 7 | passive, once a turn | a move made Hidden from cover to cover (it starts and ends next to cover) costs 1 AP less, at least 1. Item 1974 |
| Rig | 7 | 2 AP, 1 Shadow | a trap of your side on your tile or one next to it, flat 25 at level 1 (the `flat` profile); one at a time. Item 1975 |

Every verb above but Lift and the two passives needs you Hidden. **Not built** (listed in `shadow.json pending` with the
reason; item 1966): Parting Cut and Case.

### 4. The Operative (`infiltrator`; Perception)

1. **Tradecraft** (class gain): starts each fight with 1 Shadow (`operative_start`), and the meter holds 1 more
   (`operative_cap_add`: a class that brings Shadow); its Analyze costs 1 AP and puts **Read** on the target (the
   Trickster's Read folded in); once a turn, Analyzing an enemy that can't see it gives 1 Shadow. Item 1956.
2. **Rank I:** Mark (kept: 1 AP, an enemy you see is Marked to the fight's end, 3 at once; a Break on it counts the
   0.15 above); **Vanish** (kept, now data only: 1 AP once a turn, out of view, become Hidden, a new entry; not while
   Marked). Item 1957.
3. **Rank II:** **Toxin** (kept: 1 AP, a dose of `res.toxins`, restocked at rest) now coats **any** weapon, a gun's next
   rounds too; a Break with it adds the Shadow it spends to the save's TN. **Sabotage** (moved from rank III): a machine
   within 1 is Stunned **1 round** (`numbers.rounds`; was 2), no save and no Shadow; or a barricade within 1 breaks;
   or rig your tile (unchanged). Item 1958.
4. **Rank III:** **Execution** (kept) never fires on a hit the Elite and Boss guard held, nor on an Elite or Boss that
   was at full HP when the action began, whatever the level gap. **Called Shot** (moved in from the Skirmisher's pool,
   key `gunslinger.called_shot`): with any weapon (a shot, a throw, or a strike in reach), −2 to hit, **no −2 while the
   target can't see you**. Item 1959.
5. **Field Fix leaves the class** (its key `infiltrator.field_fix` stays, in the move pool, shelved, for the Rigger in
   step 8). Item 1960.

### 5. The other side

Enemies carry no Shadow meter. The Elite and Boss guard holds every roll of a Break; Execution never finishes a
guard-held or full-HP Elite in the same action (item 1959). Enemies tagged **`skulk`** (`FOE_TAGS`: Vermin, Minions and
Soldiers) Hide when out of view with no shot, and ambush from it at the flat ×1.5 (item 1961). The search of the
last-seen tile is the 0.25.0 rule, unchanged.

### 6. Balance

The line: **a three-turn window with one Break, the Operative all in = 125%** of a rifle-turn (the door all in
125 ÷ 1.15 = 109, the door at a normal share 87; `rules.json balance.ceilings.shadow`). The dial is
`rules.json shadow.per_point`, fitted only after measuring (not refitted in this step). Items 1962 to 1965.

## Rules revision 1.33: Tending, Bonds and the Mender (Classes 3.0, step 7)

Built on 13 Nov 2026 from `docs/design/bonds-spec.md` (binding; its "Settled by Leon" notes override its body) and
`docs/design/class-roster-rev4-proposal.md` section 4.7 and its last blocks. It overrides every body line on the Bard's
moves, Supplies, Inspire, Empathy's per-point text and the Outburst's free Pump that says otherwise (the class table
of rules 1.10, rules 1.19's free Pump, rules 1.23's medic kit where it names the class). The class id stays `bard`
(display name Mender, rules 1.29). Every number here is PROVISIONAL (items 2000 to 2041). Heal and shield SIZES are
step 7b's (the percent re-fit): they are built on their named dials (`output.profiles.tend`, each verb's amount block)
so 7b moves them by data alone; the Outburst's, the Sigil's and prayer's heals are not touched here.

### 1. The Attuner: a focus is data

1. **Every focus item names its door** (`items.json` `focus: {door, hand, fuel}`): the Evoker `brain_power` (fuel
   `core`), the Emanator `will_power` (fuel `mp`), and the new **Attuner** `empathy` (fuel `mp`; off hand, one hand,
   0.4 kg, 1000 credits). A rule asks for "a focus of door X in a hand" (`self_holds {slot: hand, door: empathy}`),
   never an item id; a faction's focus later is one more item. Item 2000.
2. **The Attuner in a hand** lets you Bond and use every Tending verb and every Mender move that spends MP. MP is the
   Soul's fuel: a character carrying an Emanator **or an Attuner** keeps its MP in it; spending MP through Tending
   needs the Attuner in a hand (the `mp` resource row's `needs` is "an MP focus in a hand"). **In the pack:** the
   Bonds you hold stay, you make no new Bond and use no verb, and the passives of section 2 are off. **Off your
   person:** at the next round's start every Bond you hold ends. Stims and medical kits need no focus. Item 2001.
3. **Two gloves, no weapon:** Outbursts and Tending together take both hands (an Emanator and an Attuner); the
   unarmed attack and the Release are then the damaging actions, and every rule below rides both. Item 2002.

### 2. Bonds (ties of kind `bond`)

1. **Bond** (`tending.json tend.bond`): 1 AP; a unit in your sight within `bond.make_range` (6; 9 from Empathy 6);
   anyone with Empathy 1 and an Attuner in hand. An **ally** Bond needs no roll. An **enemy** rolls a **Heart save**
   against your Empathy strength (rules 1.13), an Elite at **+2**, a Boss at **+5**; a success: no Bond, the AP is
   spent. A machine (robot, drone, turret) or a Figment can't be Bonded. Every Bonded unit bears the condition
   **Bonded** (`bonded`, the tie kind's mark: it ends with the last Bond on it, and the Bond ends with it). Item 2003.
2. **Bonds held** (`ties_max:bond`): 1 at Empathy 1, 2 at 5, 3 at 8; the Mender +1. Allies and enemies share the cap.
   A Bond past the cap is refused (let one go first: letting go is free, on your turn). Item 2004.
3. **How a Bond ends:** an ally Bond: the ally dies; you go Down (from Empathy 10 your ally Bonds hold while you are
   Downed); the fight ends. An enemy Bond: the enemy goes Down or dies; you go Down; it has been out of your sight
   for a whole round; a **Boss** Bond at the end of the Boss's third turn (`bond.boss_rounds` 3), and you can't Bond
   that Boss again for `bond.boss_gap` (4) rounds from the Bond; the fight ends; your Attuner leaves your person. No
   enemy verb tears a Bond. Item 2005.
4. **Through a Bond** (`bond.through` ×1.2): every Tending heal or shield you give a Bonded ally is ×1.2, and Tending
   reaches a Bonded ally at any range while you can see it. Unbonded, Tending reaches 3 tiles in sight (Touch:
   adjacent). Item 2006.
5. **It takes damage for you** (`bond.share` 0.20): whenever you take damage from anyone but yourself, after your
   armour and before your shield, 20% of it goes instead to your Bonded enemies, split evenly, as Soul damage that
   ignores their armour; a share is never moved again and triggers no reaction. Item 2007.
6. **You hit it more easily** (`bond.hit` +3): every roll to hit you make against an enemy Bonded to you (a weapon
   attack, a Sigil, an Outburst: the one roll hook). Allies get nothing. Item 2008.
7. **Your healing hurts it** (`bond.echo` **0.20**, Leon's number): every heal you give that restores HP to yourself or
   a Bonded ally (any source) makes each enemy Bonded to you take 20% of the HP restored, as Soul damage at the start
   of that enemy's next turn (frozen when the heal lands; armour ignored; never redirected; an echo never echoes).
   Overheal, shields, heals given to you and heals out of a fight do not count. Item 2009.
8. **The more you are tied, the harder you hit** (`bond.per_bond` 0.10): every damage you deal to an enemy by your own
   blow is ×(1 + 0.10 × the Bonds you hold). Not the share, the echo, Bleeding or Burning. Item 2010.
9. Rules 5 to 8 and the Ledger's spend need the Attuner in a hand. Item 2011.
10. **Felt at the Down:** when a Bonded ally goes Down you lose `bond.down_mp` (10) MP. Item 2012.
11. **Traced** (condition, no save, 2 rounds): given to whoever tends through a Bond, and renewed at the start of each
    of your turns while you hold an enemy Bond. While Traced you can't be Hidden and the enemies know where you are
    (`always_seen`); what you tend counts for the enemies' healer hunt (rules 1.23). Item 2013.
12. Bonds, the Ledger and the queued echoes live on the fight (`cb.ties`, the resource, `cb.delayed`); all end with
    it. Item 2014.

### 3. Tending (the verbs; `data/tending.json`)

Every verb needs the Attuner in a hand and pays MP through it; no Strain. Amounts: base × Healing given (the `tend`
profile: Insight and Empathy, 0.06 a point each, k 1.573) × the level factor (`mend`) × the through (if Bonded). Reach
"R3": an ally within 3 tiles you see, or a Bonded ally anywhere you see. A Downed ally is reached only by Raise.

| Verb | Cost | Opens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bond | 1 AP | Empathy 1 | section 2, rule 1 |
| Let go | 0 AP | Empathy 1 | end one of your Bonds |
| Mend | 2 AP, 8 MP (6 from Empathy 9) | Empathy 1 | R3 heal 3.75; on yourself once a turn (no through, no Trace) |
| Touch | 2 AP, 8 MP (6 from Empathy 9) | Empathy 1 | an adjacent ally: heal 4.3 |
| Settle | 1 AP, 5 MP | Empathy 1 | R3 or yourself: +2 on Body, Brain and Heart saves until your next turn |
| Soothe | 1 AP, 6 MP | Empathy 1 | R3 or yourself: end the newest harmful Body condition (Heart too from Empathy 5; two from Empathy 7) |
| Shield | 2 AP, 10 MP (8 from Empathy 9) | Empathy 2 | R3: a shield of 4.5 on the base layer (the larger stands) |
| Raise | 1 AP, 12 MP | Empathy 3 | a Downed ally adjacent or Bonded in sight stands at 1.9 (at least 1 HP); once a turn |
| Guide | 1 AP, 5 MP | Empathy 4 | R3: the ally steps up to 2 tiles (3 from Empathy 7) to a tile you pick; willing; provokes nothing |
| Share a Hit | reaction (protect) | Camaraderie 1 | an adjacent ally (a Bonded ally in sight from Camaraderie 5) is hit: you take 25% + 5% a point of Camaraderie of it (at most 50%); no focus |
| Field Surgery | out of a fight, a field kit, 15 MP | Empathy 3 | treat one limb injury or clear every Body condition; once an ally a scene |

Stim Throw is a gear action anyone has (1 AP, a stim, an ally within 4 you see). Songs stay gear and traits. Items
2015 to 2024.

### 4. The ladder, and what leaves Empathy

Empathy: the door at 1 (Bond, 1 Bond held, Mend, Touch, Settle, Soothe, the passives of section 2); Shield at 2; Raise,
Field Surgery and Feel Their Pain at 3; Guide at 4; 2 Bonds, Soothe reaches Heart, Mercy at 5; Bond made within 9 at 6;
Soothe ends 2, Guide 3 tiles, a perk step at 7; 3 Bonds at 8; Mend, Touch and Shield 2 MP cheaper and a perk step at
9; the Mastered perk and ally Bonds that hold while Downed at 10. Healing given grows 0.06 a point throughout.
**Empathy's free Pump (from 3) and the held Outburst's swell without Strain (from 7) move to Will Power** at the same
points (`soul_modules.json cycle`). Anyone with Empathy 1 can feel (rules 1.8's feelings); a character who first gains
it picks 2 starting feelings. The Empathy gate word is `focus:attuner`. Camaraderie: +10% healing received a point;
Share a Hit at 1 (a Bonded ally in sight from 5); Hand-Off and Nobody Left Behind kept. Insinuation: unchanged. Items
2025 to 2027.

### 5. The Mender (`bard`)

**Better:** one more Bond held (2 / 3 / 4); the first Bond action each turn costs 0 AP and has no range limit (any
unit it sees); six moves. Supplies are no longer the class's resource; its resources are MP and the Ledger.

| Rank | Move (key) | Cost | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| I | Triage (`medic.triage`) | 2 AP, 6 MP | an adjacent or Bonded ally in sight: heal 4.3 and end Bleeding; once an ally a turn; out of a fight ×3, once an ally a scene |
| I | The Ledger (`bard.ledger`) | passive | every heal you give that restores HP and every shield you give, to an ally or yourself, is counted (at most 15.5 × Healing given × level); your next damage to an enemy by your own blow, any weapon or door, adds 0.7 × the Ledger before armour and empties it; a miss spends nothing; it empties at a fight's end |
| II | Inspire (`bard.inspire`) | 1 AP, 10 MP | a Bonded unit in sight: give it a feeling you have felt (section 6) |
| II | Take the Weight (`bard.take_the_weight`) | reaction (protect) | a Bonded ally in sight would go Down: it stays at 1 HP and you lose 15% of your max HP (true damage), only while above a quarter of your max HP; or a Bonded ally would be Stunned, Dazed or Afraid: you take it instead |
| III | Brimming (`bard.mend`) | passive | Tending you give that heals past an ally's max HP leaves half the excess as a shield on it |
| III | Rally (`bard.rally`) | 2 AP, 20 MP, once a scene | every Bonded ally wherever it is and every ally within 4 heals 3.1 and loses Fear and Shaken |

`medic.stim_throw` and `medic.field_surgery` held by a Mender are dropped (both are everyone's); `res.supplies` is
dropped; a Mender at rank I has Triage and the Ledger, Inspire comes at rank II. Items 2028 to 2034.

### 6. Feelings given along a Bond (Inspire)

An ally given a feeling gets +2 on its next roll to hit (`given_edge`) and the feeling's boon (`given_<id>`) until the
end of its next turn; "next attack" parts end with that attack. An enemy gets the feeling's enemy face (`foe_<id>`),
with a Heart save against your Empathy strength where marked (Elite +2, Boss +5; a Boss is never Commanded or
Taunted by it), or nothing (10 feelings have none). One given feeling on a unit at a time; each feeling once a fight on
each unit; once a unit a round; an enemy not two rounds running. The 25 rows are `feelings.json` `given` and
`given_foe` (bonds-spec.md 5.1). Items 2035 to 2037.

### 7. The other side

Enemies do not Bond or Tend in this patch. A Bonded enemy and its Bonder both see the Bond; while you hold an enemy
Bond you are Traced (seen through walls by the hunt). The rest of the enemy AI (an Elite or Boss Bonded to you hunts
you first) is the enemy step's (Classes 3.0 step 9). Item 2038.

### 8. Balance lines

`balance.ceilings.tending_turn` 200 (the Mender's healing turn in Soldier-turns × 100; dial `output.profiles.tend.k`),
`mender_offence` 70 and `mender_window` 100 (percent of a rifle-turn; dials `bond.per_bond`, the Ledger's factor).
Measured in the step 7 hand-off, not refitted here. Items 2039 to 2041.
## Rules revision 1.34: Figments, the Visualizer and the Rigger (Classes 3.0, step 8)

Built on 13 Nov 2026 from `docs/design/figments-spec.md` (binding; its "Settled" notes override its body) and the Settled
blocks of `docs/design/class-roster-rev4-proposal.md` section 8. It overrides every body line on Visualization (its
per-point line, the unbuilt Afterimage, Paint the Field), on Field Repair and Field Fix, and on the Trickster's moves
(rules 1.10's class table, rules 1.29), where they differ. The class id stays `trickster`; its display name is the
Rigger. Every number here is PROVISIONAL (items 2100 to 2199). Data: `data/figments.json` (new), the `trickster` block of
`classes.json`, `items.json visualizer`, `weapons.json figment_claws` and `figment_edge`, `actions.json` (the resource
`vcharge`, the cost sites `picture`, `let_go`, `figment_strike`, `figment_pounce`, `figment_cut`, `figment_stare`),
`conditions.json watched`, `rules.json` (profiles `figment` and `repair`, the pair `repair`, `factors.figment`,
`balance.ceilings.figments`), `enemies.json` tiers (`owned_weight`, `double_save`), `skills.json` (Visualization's
unlocks 1, 3, 5, 7, 9; Field Repair's `amounts.repair`).

### 1. The Visualizer and Figments (Expression's door, through Visualization)

1. **The Visualizer** (`items.json visualizer`, the third standard focus; Leon: a glove with a projector set in the
   middle of the palm): off hand, holds one mana core of its own (`figments.json visualizer.charge`, 10; resource
   `vcharge`). Picturing and acting through a Figment need it **in a hand** (`self_holds {door: visualizer}`); held
   Figments stay while it is **carried**; its charge goes home with the character (`visCharge`). Its core is swapped by
   the verb `visualizer_core` (the `swap_core` site, a spare core).
2. **Picture** (verb `picture`, cost site `picture`, 2 AP; the design's charge): a Figment of a ready design or a bare
   form opened appears on a free tile the owner's side sees within **projection range** (`visualizer.range`: 4 + 1 a
   point of Visualization; a Rigger without the door 6, for its Double). Its charge is the form's + 1 a trait
   (`trait_charge`) + each trait's own (Hollow −2), at least 1.
3. **Held** (`ladder`): 1 at Visualization 1, 2 at 5, 3 at 7; the Rigger +1 (stat `ties_max:owned`), never past
   `limits.held_most` (4). Past it Picture is refused ("Hold is full: let one go first").
4. **Upkeep** (`upkeep`): 1 charge a held Figment at its owner's turn start (the owned unit's `upkeep`, P9); holding 3 or
   more also costs 1 AP that turn. Short of charge, the newest unravels.
5. **Acting through** (owned units of turn `owner`, rules 1.28 items 1768, 1769): a Figment's verbs are rows of its
   owner's panel, priced at their cost site on the owner and paid from the owner's AP. The Visualizer in hand, not
   Silenced, the Figment within projection range (Tethered: +4). Its attack rolls d20 + the owner's Visualization
   modifier (Keen +2); its damage is its weapon's on the profile `figment` (k 1.5, the Level term `deal` at the owner's
   level) times **the Figment factor** (`output.factors.figment`, 0.9).
6. **Let go** (verb `let_go`, 0 AP): unmade; half its charge (`refund_share` 0.5, rounded down) goes back. A Figment
   **destroyed** by damage gives nothing back and its owner **Snaps**: 1 AP less next turn (`let_go.snap_ap`; at most
   once a turn; not from Visualization 9). A destroyed Figment releases no mana and spills no Pressure (it is no one's
   death).
7. **Attention breaks**: the owner Downed or Stunned: every Figment unravels, nothing back. Silenced: no Picture and no
   acting through; they stay. A Figment that ends its owner's turn beyond projection range (Tethered: twice it)
   unravels. The fight's end unravels every Figment and Scrap Turret.
8. **What a Figment is**: a unit of its owner's side with HP, Defense, armour and a pace; no turn, no AP, no reactions
   of its own; immune to every condition (the Body, Brain and Heart families, Bleeding: `figments.json unit_effects`, held
   as the item `fig_<form>`); the Wall is immune to knockback. Its level numbers: HP × `hp_mult × damage_mult`, Defense +
   `defense_plus`, armour × `armour_mult` at the owner's level (`figments.json level`).
9. **Sight**: only the Eye sees for its side (`eyes`; vision 8, dark sight); the other forms see nothing.
10. **The Blade's Hold**: the first enemy each round to enter or leave a tile next to a Blade is Cut; that spends one of
    the owner's reactions (`react()`, kind `attack`, payer the owner); with none left it does not strike.
11. **Designs** (`Character.figments`): a form and its traits, named, kept out of a fight: 2 ready at Visualization 3, 3
    at 5, 4 at 8, 5 at 10 (the Rigger +1, stat `figment_designs`); one trait a design from 3, two from 7. A bare form
    opened is always ready.

### 2. The forms and the traits (`figments.json forms`, `traits`)

| Form | Opens | Charge | HP / Defense / armour (level 1) | Tiles an AP | Verbs (cost site, AP) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Double | Vis 1 | 2 | 30 / the owner's / 0 | the owner's | Move; lures (section 3) |
| Eye | Vis 3 | 2 | 15 / 15 / 0 | 4, flies | Move; Stare (`figment_stare`, 1): the target is Watched (`watched`: stat `always_seen`) for a round |
| Wall | Vis 3 | 3 | 60 / 6 / 5 | 1 | Move; full cover, blocks sight, unpushable |
| Beast | Vis 5 | 4 | 45 / 12 / 3 | 3 | Move; Strike (`figment_strike`, 2: `figment_claws` 30); Pounce (`figment_pounce`, 3): up to 3 tiles in a straight line, then a Strike; a hit: Prone (Body save) |
| Blade | Vis 5 | 3 | 25 / 14 / 0 | 2 | Move; Cut (`figment_cut`, 2: `figment_edge` 25); Hold (rule 10) |

Traits (+1 charge each): Armoured (HP ×1.5), Swift (+2 tiles an AP), Loud (`figWeight` −1: every tier counts it the
most hurt), Volatile (destroyed: 20 flat, radius 1, both sides), Tethered (+4 range), Mirror (lures as a Double),
Barbed (a melee hit on it: 10 true back), Lasting (no upkeep), Keen (+2 to hit; an Eye sees 4 further), Hollow (−2
charge, HP ×0.5).

### 3. The enemies and the Double (rules 1.25's doctrine)

A Double (or a Mirror) is an image with a body (`illusion.ts FalseImage.body`). Every enemy that sees its tile when it is
made is fooled with no save if its tier's `double_save` is none (Vermin, Minion), else makes a Brain save against 12 +
the owner's Visualization strength with its tier's `double_save` added to its roll (Soldier 0, Elite 2, Boss 3) and 5
more once it has found a Double out this fight (`lure.found_out_add`). An Elite saves again at each of its turn starts; a
Boss is never fooled past its next turn start. A fooled enemy sees the owner where the Double stands (the healer hunt
included); its attack lands on the Double and finds it out. A destroyed Double is found out by all. Every tier also
weighs a Figment by its `owned_weight` in its choice of target (0 Vermin and Minion, 0.5 Soldier and Elite, 1 Boss:
a character comes first at equal hurt); Loud lowers that by 1.

### 4. Improvisation and Charisma

**Field Repair** (Improvisation 3; `field_repair`, 2 AP and one spare part) is one action with three ways, on the
repairer or a unit of its side next to it: clear a jam; restore weapon durability (10% + 5% a point above 3, as
before); **repair** a robot, drone, turret, Factory Made squadmate or Figment for `amounts.repair` 15 on the profile
`repair` (k 1.392, Expression and Improvisation, the Level term `mend`; a repair, not a heal; a Downed machine comes
back up). Factory Made's own repair amount no longer applies to Field Repair (it is the one amount). **Charisma**: no
number (the Call through the Double is not built: section 7).

### 5. The Rigger (`classes.json trickster`)

Better: one more Figment held and one more design (the class `gain` "The Rigger's Hands"); Overclock is its "one thing a
turn cheaper"; six moves, none needing Visualization:

| Rank | Key | Move | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| I | `trickster.false_image` | **Double** | 2 AP and 1 charge, the Visualizer in hand: a bare Double within projection range (6 without the door), outside the held count, no upkeep, gone at the owner's turn start 2 rounds on; one at a time |
| I | `infiltrator.field_fix` | **Field Fix** | 2 AP: Field Repair with no part and no Improvisation gate, reach 2, its own `amounts.repair` 15 |
| II | `trickster.salvage` | **Salvage** | 1 AP, next to you: a wreck (a destroyed machine of either side) gives 2 charge (each wreck once a fight); or one of your Figments is let go with all its charge back; or a repair of 15 |
| II | `trickster.overclock` | **Overclock** | 1 AP, once a turn: a Figment, robot, drone or turret of your side within 8 that your side sees attacks the nearest enemy it can reach now, at no AP (an attack of up to 2 AP); it takes 5 true (the Level term `deal`). Never a character |
| III | `trickster.sleight` | **Sleight** | 1 AP, once a scene: swap places with one of your Figments or a standing ally within 6 |
| III | `trickster.scrap_turret` | **Scrap Turret** (was Jury-Rig) | 3 AP, once a scene, one at a time: from a wreck, a pile with a weapon or a barricade next to you, a turret (`figments.json turret`: 40 HP, Defense 10, armour 5, no move; an owned unit of turn `auto`) that at each of your turn starts for 3 rounds makes its weapon's plain attack (the wreck's or pile's weapon, else the service pistol) at the nearest enemy it can reach, d20 + your Improvisation modifier, the weapon profile at your level |

Leave the class (keys kept in the move pool, shelved): Silver Tongue, Blind and Slow, Rewrite. Read goes to the Operative
(on this step's branch it stands in the Operative's rank II where Field Fix was; the Shadow step sets that rank).

### 6. The balance line

`rules.json balance.ceilings.figments`: the Rigger all in **150** (two Figments), the door all in 130, at a normal share
104; the Rigger at a normal share 120. Dial: `output.factors.figment` (0.9), then `figments.json level.hp`. Measured in
`docs/design/handoffs/classes-3.0-step-8.md`.

### 7. Not built in this revision

The Call spoken through a Double (spec rule 15); NULL unmaking Figments (`sigils.json null.dispel`); a Wall's cover and
sight-blocking for both sides as standing cover (the owned block's `cover` is half cover today); the Volatile burst's
both-sides area on a Figment's own fall is data (`figtrait_volatile`); the Visualizer out of a fight (rule 17, a
Narrator's check); the AI's handling beyond the Double's saves and `owned_weight` (section 8 of the spec: the enemy step).
## Rules revision 1.35: the katana, and the Emanator katana held back (a test of adding a weapon by data alone)

Built on 13 Nov 2026 (Leon: "add as weapon, test out our add-weapon capability in this engine"); the art is in the
13 Nov gear delivery (`weapon-katana`, `weapon-emanator_katana`). Lead's numbers, Leon to confirm: every number here is
PROVISIONAL (items 2200 to 1956).

### 1. The katana (built: `data/weapons.json` `katana`)

A long one-handed cutting blade, so a **light blade** (7.7): it hits with Dexterity and scales with Agility, 2 AP a
strike, properties light and edge, mastery family light blades, durability 250, mod slots edge and grip, no
requirement. Every number sits inside the family's range, nearest the **sabre** (the comparable weapon): damage 28
(the family's top, the sabre's), 1.4 kg (sabre 1.5), 500 credits (between the sabre's 400 and the duelling blade's
550). It lends **Draw Cut** (an existing technique: draw it from the pack and strike in one action; Bleeding on a hit
from its edge), and has every technique its properties give (Cut, the light and edge lines). No weapon skill of its own
(no `grants`), no martial art, no new technique (Leon shelved those for an advanced class). It is in no loot table:
the sabre, its comparable, is in none.

### 2. The Emanator katana (designed, NOT built)

The Soul twin of the Evoker blade (7.11): a one-handed blade that **counts as an Emanator**, needs Will Power 3, and
takes the Evoker blade's numbers (26 damage, 1H, 1.8 kg, 2,400 credits); each hit adds 1 to the ambient mana as every
mana arm's does. It is **held back** because the engine cannot be told by data that a weapon counts as an Emanator: the
focus gate reads a list written in code (`FOCUS_IDS` in `packages/engine/src/character.ts`), not the weapon's
`counts_as_emanator` property. It goes into 7.11 and the data the day the focus list is read from data (items 2205, 1956).
*Built by rules 1.38 (point 2): the focus list is read from data, and the Emanator katana is data alone.*

## Rules revision 1.36: the level scale, and healing and shields in percent of HP (Classes 3.0, step 7b)

Built on 13 Nov 2026 from `docs/design/level-scale-spec.md` and `docs/design/heal-shield-percent-spec.md`, each with its
"Settled by Leon" block (which overrides its body). Every number here is PROVISIONAL (items 2300 to 2335). The hand-off
is `docs/design/handoffs/classes-3.0-step-7b.md`.

### 1. The level scale (Leon: a plain rifle hit is 40 at level 1, as before, and about 300 at level 20)

1. **Damage grows ×7.5 from level 1 to level 20, geometric by level:** `output.level.deal` = 7.5^((level − 1)/19)
   (×1.112 a level: 1 at level 1, 1.53 at 5, 2.60 at 10, 7.5 at 20). The plain rifle's hit on a Soldier of its level
   is 40 at level 1, 60 at 5, 103 at 10, 299 at 20.
2. **`output.level.scale`** is the new `deal` over rules 1.26's (1 at level 1, 1.27 at 5, 1.77 at 10, 4.69 at 20). It
   is what **everything measured in HP** is multiplied by, so every ratio between a hit and what it hits is as before:
   - **players' max HP** = round(scale × (100 + 15 × (Endurance − 1) + (level − 1) × (5 + 2 × Pain Threshold))), perks
     and traits inside the bracket (145 / 233 / 441 / 2,086 for the reference rifleman at levels 1 / 5 / 10 / 20);
   - **enemies**: the table's HP, armour and damage columns (`enemies.json levels.table`) × scale: a Soldier at level
     20 has 1,188 HP and 38 armour, an Elite 2,036 and 75, a Boss 6,957 and 75; companions and owned units read the
     same rows at their owner's level;
   - **players' armour** (a Class's 5 to 25, what gear and items add) × scale at the wearer's level; armour a hit breaks
     or a technique ignores (a weapon's armour break, Half-Sword, a heavy bolt's pierce, a weapon's armour-ignore) ×
     scale at the striker's level;
   - **Guard's soak** (10 a point) × scale at the holder's level; **Strain's burn** (8 a point), Shame's self-damage,
     a feeling's residue and the Aura's tick × scale at the caster's level;
   - **cover and objects** at the fight's level (an object remembers the level its HP is in, so one carried from a
     fight to the story and back moves once); a RAISE wall at its maker's level;
   - the profiles that had no Level term (`physical`, `elemental`, `healing`, `blessing`: prayer damage, Smite, the
     interventions, the school riders) read `scale`;
   - flat things made by nobody (a hazard, a map trap, a barrel) read the enemy table's damage column, as before.
3. **What does not scale:** to-hit, Defense, attack bonuses, criticals' multipliers, AP, **MP** (a pool and its costs
   are one unit), Flux, cores, credits, XP, every percent and every ratio (the balance contract's lines), and the
   1-damage floor of a hit (a Vermin's bite on plate stays 1). **Level 1 is unchanged to the digit.**
4. A share of max HP or of a hit carries no Level term (or it would grow twice): Shrug It Off, Clean Hands, Field
   Surgeon and Crawler-Blooded's chitin drop the `flat` profile they had.
5. **Old saves:** a character saved before this revision keeps the same share of its bar (current HP × scale at its
   level, held to the new max), once; a fight saved mid-way moves its units' HP, max HP, shields and armour and its
   objects' HP the same way. A level-up adds the rise in max HP to current HP (rules 1.11's "+HP a level", in the new
   units).

### 2. Heals and shields in percent of HP

1. **The unit:** percent of the reference character's max HP (`output.level.reference_hp`: the normal-share plain
   rifleman, smoothed, × scale: 145 at level 1, 2,086 at 20) restored or shielded by one whole turn spent on the source,
   all in.
2. **The heal Level term** is its own column, `output.level.mend` = M(L) × scale(L) (M keeps an all-in heal turn on
   the same percent at every level: 1 at level 1, 1.51 at 5, 2.53 at 10, 11.97 at 20); it no longer reads the enemy
   table.
3. **The lines, all in** (`rules.json balance`): the Mender's turn through Bonds 65 (a door user about 59); an
   off-heal (the Outburst's Buff school, steady; a Sigil MEND Line of three glyphs) 45; a Whisper 15; a Hymn's turn 65
   at most, about 45 averaged over its wait.
4. **The gate:** every heal and shield action gives at least a share of its target's max HP, counted up to 145 ×
   scale at the giver's level: **20% for a 2-AP action** (the `mend`, `sigil_mend`, `soul_mend` and `tend` profiles),
   13.3% for a Whisper and a 1-AP Raise, 33.3% for a Hymn and an intervention, times the action's own multipliers (an
   Outburst's stage, a shape's share, a heal in an area ×0.4, a rider's half). It rounds up. The 125-HP level 1
   Recruit with no Soul skill heals **25** with one quick heal (stage 1) and **40** fully pumped (stage 4, plain).
5. **The cap:** no single heal restores more than **half its target's max HP**; a Miracle is exempt; a shield has
   none (one stands per layer).
6. **A stim** heals 20% of its target's max HP, the whole bar counted (the gate alone; gear, priced in credits).
7. **The new numbers:** the Buff heal 11.3 on the Outburst's own Stat (`soul_mend`: Will Power and Determination; it
   no longer reads Healing given); Sigil MEND 15 and WARD 4.3, the boon on the Sigil's own Stat (`sigil_mend.k` 1.629
   carries what Healing given did); Inverse 7 (Shell 4 kept); Whisper Health 8.5 and Protection 10; Warm Hands 28,
   Saint's Shield 34, Absolution 19, Coin for the Ferry 11, Hearthlight 9; Mother Ember's intervention 7 + 2.1 ×
   Devotion, with the heal Level term, the intervention's gate and the cap; Tending's `tend.k` 3.74; the Ledger's cap
   6.5 (its factor 0.7 and the echo 0.20 kept); Sanctuary's pool 40; Ward 10 (as rules 1.31).
8. **The shields' order** (Leon: the strongest shield in the game is Faith's): Faith's strongest single use
   (Sanctuary's pool: about two full assaults, 70% of the reference HP all in) = 1; the Mender's Tending shield about
   0.36 of it; the Sigil WARD Line and the Outburst's Inverse about 0.33. **A full assault** is what the fire doctrine
   (rules 1.25) puts on one character in a round of the standard encounter (55 HP at level 1, × scale).

### 3. The fits made with the same dials

- **Shadow:** `shadow.per_point` 0.15 → 0.7 (the door all in about 107 against its 109, the Operative about 121
  against 125).
- **Figments:** a Figment's HP follows its maker: its form's HP × `figment_hp` (0.35 × (1 + 0.15 × Visualization's
  points)) × the enemy table's `hp_mult` at its owner's level (the `damage_mult` term is gone: both columns carry the
  scale now).
- **The Mender's offence:** the Ledger's cap 15.5 → 6.5 (its HP as before under `tend.k` 3.74).

Supersedes: rules 1.26's `deal` column (item 1703); rules 1.15's three enemy columns; the HP line of "The game in one
screen"; rules 1.20's level factor and bases; rules 1.23's stim; rules 1.27 (the 2.0 Soldier-turn ceiling, the Hymn
heal cap of 250); rules 1.33's `tend.k` 1.573 and the Ledger's 15.5; rules 1.32's `per_point` 0.15.

## Rules revision 1.37: what enemies do about the new systems (Classes 3.0, step 9)

Built on 13 Nov 2026 (Classes 3.0 step 9; `docs/design/handoffs/classes-3.0-step-9.md`): section 8, "The other side",
of the reaction, Chaplain, Shadow, Bonds and Figments specs. The AI's own numbers are in `data/enemies.json` `ai`
(behaviour only: no HP or damage). Every number is PROVISIONAL (items 2400 to 2412). It overrides the limit written
in item 1744 ("an enemy still knows where every hostile who is not Hidden stands").

### 1. An enemy acts on what its side perceives

1. **Targets.** An enemy's targets, its approach, its healer hunt and its Sigil and Soul planners read only the
   hostiles its side sees now (the fog's answer: in some eye's Vision and line of sight, not Hidden, or always seen:
   Traced, Watched). One it can't see is no target and no tile to close on; a False Image or a Double it was fooled by
   stays its belief, as before. An area it plans counts only the hostiles it sees.
2. **The opening.** A fight opens because the sides met: when the set-up is done (who starts Hidden is Hidden), each
   side knows the tile of every hostile that is not Hidden, seen or not. From then on a side knows only what it sees,
   and where it last saw each hostile (item 1744).
3. **Searching.** An enemy that sees nobody walks toward the nearest tile its side believes a hostile is on (fewest
   tiles of walk): a Hidden one's last-seen tile (or the tile a Decoy gave), else the last tile its side saw the
   hostile on. It ends its walk there; standing on it with nothing in sight it holds (it has searched there; ending
   next to a Hidden one finds it, as before). It never walks toward where the hostile really is.
4. **Heard, not seen.** A unit hit by an attacker its side can't see learns the attacker's tile: its side's last-seen
   tile of the attacker becomes the attacker's tile (a Hidden attacker's search tile too).
5. **No fire at a tile.** No rule allows an enemy to shoot at a tile it believes someone is on (suppressive fire); it
   never does.
6. **The spot-back** is the side's: a Hidden character one enemy spots is seen by its whole side at once and is a
   target for all of them (the call-out is shared sight).

### 2. Shadow

7. **A skulker flanks.** A Vermin, Minion or Soldier with the tag `skulk` that closes in adds `ai.skulk_open` (3) to
   every tile the other side has in view: it reaches its target through what the other side can't see when it can
   (it still Hides with no shot and out of view, and ambushes, rules 1.32).
8. **A Boss is never Hidden after round 1** (`ai.boss_hidden_rounds`, 1): from round 2 it can't Hide (the action, a
   condition, an item), and one the Narrator placed Hidden is revealed as round 2 starts. Elites may still be placed
   Hidden.
9. **Never one-shot from Shadow:** unchanged (rules 1.32: the guard holds every roll of a Break; Execution never on a
   guard-held hit).
10. **A Marked enemy** behaves as any enemy: Marked changes what the Operative's side knows, not the AI (nothing new).

### 3. Bonds

11. **The Bonded enemy knows the tie** (`ai.healer_tie`, `bond`): an enemy at the far end of a Bond counts its Bonder
    as the other side's healer whatever it has healed, before any other healer: an Elite or a Boss (`healer_focus` 1)
    turns on it first and steps for a line on it; a Soldier (0.5) leans to it; a Minion does not look. Taunt still
    comes first.
12. **Enemies do not Bond, Tend, hold a Shadow meter or make Figments** in this patch: no tier, caster or companion
    carries an Attuner, a Visualizer, a door skill of the new systems or a Shadow resource.
13. **An ally that will be Raised** is not weighed (no spec rule names it): the doctrine is unchanged.

### 4. Figments

14. **Figments last** (`ai.figments_last`: Soldiers, Elites, Bosses): such an enemy takes a Figment only when no
    character is in reach, and sizes up no Figment while one is. A Loud Figment draws every tier, and a Double that
    fooled it is its owner to it (item 2171). Vermin and Minions take the nearest thing, a Figment included.
15. **A Wall** that blocks an enemy's only way closer is broken like a RAISE wall (it is a unit: the enemy attacks it);
    otherwise its path goes round it.
16. **A Blade's Hold** the enemy's side can see is a held attack (rule 18); **a Volatile Figment** it sees prices the
    tiles next to it the same (its burst).
17. **NULL on a Figment** is not weighed: NULL does not unmake Figments yet (figments-spec rule 12 is not built).

### 5. The Chaplain and reactions

18. **Held attacks it can see** (`ai.held_risk`, 10, Anchor's weight): a walk that would spring an Overwatch or a
    Killzone (the holder sees a tile of it within its weapon's reach) or a Blade's Hold (it steps into or out of the
    Blade's reach) costs this much more, once a holder; so where a walk avoids it at no cost, the enemy takes that
    walk. A holder it can't perceive (Hidden) is unknown to it.
19. **A Warded or sheltered target is a worse target:** to the doctrine's "most hurt" a target's shield layers count as
    HP, and a target standing in a zone of its own side whose kind is in `ai.shelter` (a Sanctuary: 2) counts as that
    many times its HP. Walking into the other side's Sanctuary is no risk (it shelters only its owner's side).
